G5100.pos:
1. a certain, a certain one
  2. some, some time, a while
G5100.def: an enclitic indefinite pronoun; some or any person or object:--a (kind of), any (man, thing, thing at all), certain (thing), divers, he (every) man, one (X thing), ought, + partly, some (man, -body, - thing, -what), (+ that no-)thing, what(-soever), × wherewith, whom(-soever), whose(-soever).

G5101.def: probably emphatic of «5100»; an interrogative pronoun, who, which or what (in direct or indirect questions):--every man, how (much), + no(-ne, thing), what (manner, thing), where (-by, -fore, -of, -unto, - with, -withal), whether, which, who(-m, -se), why.

G5102.def: of Latin origin; a titulus or "title" (placard):--title.

G5103.et: of Latin origin but uncertain signification
G5103.def: of Latin origin but uncertain significance; Titus, a Christian:--Titus.

G5104.et: probably for the dative case of (3588)
G5104.def: probably for the dative case of «3588»; an enclitic particle of asseveration by way of contrast; in sooth:--(used only with other particles in the comparative, as «2544», «3305», «5105», «5106», etc.)

G5105.pos: 1. wherefore then, for which reason, therefore, consequently
G5105.def: from «5104» and «1063» and «3767»; truly for then, i.e. consequently:--there-(where-)fore.

G5106.def: from «5104» and «3568»; truly now, i.e. accordingly:--then, therefore.

G5107.def: (including the other inflections); from a derivative of 5104 and «1161»; such-like then, i.e. so great:--such.

G5108.def: (including the other inflections); from «5104» and «3778»; truly this, i.e. of this sort (to denote character or individuality):--like, such (an one).

G5110.def: from the base of «5088»; interest on money loaned (as a produce):--usury.

G5111.et: from tolma (boldness, probably itself from the base of (5056) through the idea of extreme conduct)
G5111.def: from tolma (boldness; probably itself from the base of «5056» through the idea of extreme conduct); to venture (objectively or in act; while «2292» is rather subjective or in feeling); by implication, to be courageous:--be bold, boldly, dare, durst.

G5112.et: neuter of the compound of a derivative of the base of (5111) (as adverb)
G5112.def: neuter of the compound of a derivative of the base of 5111 (as adverb); more daringly, i.e. with greater confidence than otherwise:--the more boldly.

G5114.et: comparative of a derivative of the primary temno (to cut, more comprehensive or decisive than (2875), as if by a single stroke, whereas that implies repeated blows, like hacking)
G5114.def: comparative of a derivative of the primary temno (to cut; more comprehensive or decisive than «2875», as if by a single stroke; whereas that implies repeated blows, like hacking); more keen:--sharper.

G5115.def: from the base of «5088»; a bow (apparently as the simplest fabric):--bow.

G5116.et: from a presumed derivative (alternately) of topazos (a "topaz", of uncertain origin)
G5116.def: neuter of a presumed derivative (alternately) of topazos (a "topaz"; of uncertain origin); a gem, probably the chrysolite:--topaz.

G5117.def: apparently a primary word; a spot (general in space, but limited by occupancy; whereas «5561» is a large but participle locality), i.e. location (as a position, home, tract, etc.); figuratively, condition, opportunity; specially, a scabbard:--coast, licence, place, × plain, quarter, + rock, room, where.

G5118.et: from tosos (so much, apparently from (3588) and (3739)) and (3778) (including its variations)
G5118.def: from tosos (so much; apparently from «3588» and «3739») and «3778» (including its variations); so vast as this, i.e. such (in quantity, amount, number of space):--as large, so great (long, many, much), these many.

G5119.def: from (the neuter of) «3588» and «3753»; the when, i.e. at the time that (of the past or future, also in consecution):--that time, then.

G5120.def: properly, the genitive case of «3588»; sometimes used for «5127»; of this person:--his.

G5121.et: contraction for the neuter of (3588) and (1726)
G5121.def: contraction for the neuter of «3588» and «1726»; on the contrary:--contrariwise.

G5122.et: contraction for the neuter of (3588) and (3686)
G5122.def: contraction for the neuter of «3588» and «3686»; the name (is):--named.

G5123.def: contraction for «5124» and «2076»; that is:--that is (to say).

G5124.et: neuter singular nominative or accusative case of (3778)
G5124.def: neuter singular nominative or accusative case of «3778»; that thing:--here (-unto), it, partly, self(-same), so, that (intent), the same, there(-fore, -unto), this, thus, where(-fore).

G5125.et: dative case plural masculine or neuter of (3778)
G5125.def: dative case plural masculine or neuter of «3778»; to (for, in, with or by) these (persons or things):--such, them, there(-in, -with), these, this, those.

G5126.def: accusative case singular masculine of «3778»; this (person, as objective of verb or preposition):--him, the same, that, this.

G5127.et: genitive case singular masculine or neuter of (3778)
G5127.def: genitive case singular masculine or neuter of «3778»; of (from or concerning) this (person or thing):--here(-by), him, it, + such manner of, that, thence(-forth), thereabout, this, thus.

G5128.def: accusative case plural masculine of «3778»; these (persons, as objective of verb or preposition):--such, them, these, this.

G5129.et: dative case singular masculine or neuter of (3778)
G5129.def: dative case singular masculine or neuter of «3778»; to (in, with or by) this (person or thing):--here(-by, -in), him, one, the same, there(-in), this.

G5130.et: genitive case plural masculine or neuter of (3778)
G5130.def: genitive case plural masculine or neuter of «3778»; of (from or concerning) these (persons or things):--such, their, these (things), they, this sort, those.

G5131.def: from the base of «5176»; a he-goat (as a gnawer):--goat.

G5132.def: probably contracted from «5064» and «3979»; a table or stool (as being four-legged), usually for food (figuratively, a meal); also a counter for money (figuratively, a broker's office for loans at interest):--bank, meat, table.

G5134.et: from the base of titrosko (to wound
G5134.def: from the base of titrosko (to wound; akin to the base of «2352», «5147», «5149», etc.); a wound:--wound.

G5136.def: from «5137»; to seize by the throat or neck, i.e. to expose the gullet of a victim for killing (generally, to lay bare):--opened.

G5137.et: probably from (5143) (through the idea of mobility)
G5137.def: probably from «5143» (through the idea of mobility); the throat (neck), i.e. (figuratively) life:--neck.

G5138.et: perhaps strengthened from the base of (4486) (as if jagged by rents)
G5138.def: perhaps strengthened from the base of «4486» (as if jagged by rents); uneven, rocky (reefy):--rock, rough.

G5139.def: from a derivative of «5138»; rough district; Trachonitis, a region of Syria:--Trachonitis.

G5141.def: strengthened from a primary treo (to "dread", "terrify"); to "tremble" or fear:--be afraid, trembling.

G5142.pos:
1. to nourish, support
  2. feed
  3. to give suck, to fatten
  4. to bring up, nurture
G5142.def: a primary verb (properly, threpho; but perhaps strengthened from the base of «5157» through the idea of convolution); properly, to stiffen, i.e. fatten (by implication, to cherish (with food, etc.), pamper, rear):--bring up, feed, nourish.

G5143.et: apparently a primary verb (properly, threcho, cf (2359)), which uses dremo {drem'-o} (the base of (1408)) as alternate in certain tenses
G5143.def: apparently a primary verb (properly, threcho; compare «2359»); which uses dremo drem'-o (the base of «1408») as alternate in certain tenses; to run or walk hastily (literally or figuratively):--have course, run.

G5145.def: plural from «5140» and «1540»; three hundred:--three hundred.

G5146.def: from «5140» and «956»; properly, a crow-foot (three-pronged obstruction in war), i.e. (by analogy) a thorny plant (caltrop):--brier, thistle.

G5147.et: from tribo (to "rub", akin to teiro, truo, and the base of (5131), (5134))
G5147.def: from tribo (to "rub"; akin to teiro, truo, and the base of «5131», «5134»); a rut or worn track:--path.

G5148.def: from a compound of «5140» and «2094»; a three years' period (triennium):--space of three years.

G5149.def: apparently a primary verb; to creak (squeak), i.e. (by analogy) to grate the teeth (in frenzy):--gnash.

G5150.et: neuter of a compound of (5140) and (3376) as noun
G5150.def: neuter of a compound of «5140» and «3376» as noun; a three months' space:--three months.

G5151.def: adverb from «5140»; three times:--three times, thrice.

G5152.et: neuter of a compound of (5140) and (4721) as noun
G5152.def: neuter of a compound of «5140» and «4721» as noun; a third roof (story):--third loft.

G5153.def: from «5151» and «5507»; three times a thousand:--three thousand.

G5154.def: ordinal from «5140»; third; neuter (as noun) a third part, or (as adverb) a (or the) third time, thirdly:--third(-ly).

G5155.def: from «2359»; hairy, i.e. made of hair (mohair):--of hair.

G5156.def: from «5141»; a "trembling", i.e. quaking with fear:--+ tremble(-ing).

G5157.et: from an apparently primary trepo {to turn}
G5157.def: from an apparently primary trepo to turn; a turn ("trope"), i.e. revolution (figuratively, variation):--turning.

G5158.def: from the same as «5157»; a turn, i.e. (by implication) mode or style (especially with preposition or relative prefix as adverb, like); figuratively, deportment or character:--(even) as, conversation, (+ like) manner, (+ by any) means, way.

G5159.def: from «5158» and «5409»; to endure one's habits:--suffer the manners.

G5160.def: from «5142»; nourishment (literally or figuratively); by implication, rations (wages):--food, meat.

G5163.def: from «5164»; a track (as a wheel-rut), i.e. (figuratively) a course of conduct:--path.

G5164.def: from «5143»; a wheel (as a runner), i.e. (figuratively) a circuit of physical effects:--course.

G5165.et: from a presumed derivative of uncertain affinity
G5165.def: neuter of a presumed derivative of uncertain affinity; a bowl:--dish.

G5166.et: from a derivative of trugo (to dry) meaning ripe fruit (as if dry)
G5166.def: from a derivative of trugo (to dry) meaning ripe fruit (as if dry); to collect the vintage:--gather.

G5167.et: from truzo (to murmur; akin to (5149), but denoting a duller sound)
G5167.def: from truzo (to murmur; akin to «5149», but denoting a duller sound); a turtle-dove (as cooing):--turtle-dove.

G5168.et: from a derivative of truo (to wear away, akin to the base of (5134), (5147) and (5176))
G5168.def: from a derivative of truo (to wear away; akin to the base of «5134», «5147» and «5176»); an orifice, i.e. needle's eye:--eye. Compare «5169».

G5169.et: from a derivative of the base of (5168)
G5169.def: from a derivative of the base of «5168»; an aperture, i.e. a needle's eye:--eye.

G5170.def: from «5172»; luxurious; Tryphoena, a Christian woman:--Tryphena.

G5171.def: from «5172»; to indulge in luxury:--live in pleasure.

G5172.et: from thrupto (to break up or [figuratively] enfeeble, especially the mind and body by indulgence)
G5172.def: from thrupto (to break up or (figuratively) enfeeble, especially the mind and body by indulgence); effeminacy, i.e. luxury or debauchery:--delicately, riot.

G5173.def: from «5172»; luxuriating; Tryphosa, a Christian female:--Tryphosa.

G5174.def: from Tros (a Trojan); the Troad (or plain of Troy), i.e. Troas, a place in Asia Minor:--Troas.

G5175.def: of uncertain derivation; Trogyllium, a place in Asia Minor:--Trogyllium.

G5176.et: probably strengthened from a collateral form of the base of (5134) and (5147) through the idea of corrosion or wear, or perhaps rather of a base of (5167) and (5149) through the idea of a crunching sound
G5176.def: probably strengthened from a collateral form of the base of «5134» and «5147» through the idea of corrosion or wear; or perhaps rather of a base of «5167» and «5149» through the idea of a craunching sound; to gnaw or chew, i.e. (generally) to eat:--eat.

G5177.et: probably for an obsolete tucho (for which the middle voice of another alternate teucho [to make ready or bring to pass] is used in certain tenses, akin to the base of (5088) through the idea of effecting
G5177.def: probably for an obsolete tucho (for which the middle voice of another alternate teucho (to make ready or bring to pass) is used in certain tenses; akin to the base of «5088» through the idea of effecting; properly, to affect; or (specially), to hit or light upon (as a mark to be reached), i.e. (transitively) to attain or secure an object or end, or (intransitively) to happen (as if meeting with); but in the latter application only impersonal (with «1487»), i.e. perchance; or (present participle) as adjective, usual (as if commonly met with, with «3756», extraordinary), neuter (as adverb) perhaps; or (with another verb) as adverb, by accident (as it were):--be, chance, enjoy, little, obtain,

G5178.et: from a derivative of (5180) (meaning a drum, "tympanum")
G5178.def: from a derivative of «5180» (meaning a drum, "tympanum"); to stretch on an instrument of torture resembling a drum, and thus beat to death:--torture.

G5179.def: from «5180»; a die (as struck), i.e. (by implication) a stamp or scar; by analogy, a shape, i.e. a statue, (figuratively) style or resemblance; specially, a sampler ("type"), i.e. a model (for imitation) or instance (for warning):--en-(ex-)ample, fashion, figure, form, manner, pattern, print.

G5180.et: a primary verb (in a strengthened form)
G5180.def: a primary verb (in a strengthened form); to "thump", i.e. cudgel or pummel (properly, with a stick or bastinado), but in any case by repeated blows; thus differing from «3817» and «3960», which denote a (usually single) blow with the hand or any instrument, or «4141» with the fist (or a hammer), or «4474» with the palm; as well as from «5177», an accidental collision); by implication, to punish; figuratively, to offend (the conscience):--beat, smite, strike, wound.

G5181.et: a provincial form of the derivative of the base of (2962)
G5181.def: a provincial form of the derivative of the base of «2962»; a "tyrant"; Tyrannus, an Ephesian:--Tyrannus.

G5182.et: from turbe (Latin turba, a crowd, akin to (2351))
G5182.def: from turbe (Latin turba, a crowd; akin to «2351»); to make "turbid", i.e. disturb:--trouble.

G5183.def: from «5184»; a Tyrian, i.e. inhabitant of Tyrus:--of Tyre.

G5184.def: of Hebrew origin («06865»): Tyrus (i.e. Tsor), a place in Palestine:--Tyre.

G5185.def: from, «5187»; opaque (as if smoky), i.e. (by analogy) blind (physically or mentally):--blind.

G5186.def: from «5185»; to make blind, i.e. (figuratively) to obscure:--blind.

G5187.def: from a derivative of «5188»; to envelop with smoke, i.e. (figuratively) to inflate with self-conceit:--high-minded, be lifted up with pride, be proud.

G5188.def: apparently a primary verb; to make a smoke, i.e. slowly consume without flame:--smoke.

G5189.def: from a derivative of «5188»; stormy (as if smoky):--tempestuous.

G5190.def: from a derivative of «5177»; fortuitous, i.e. fortunate; Tychicus, a Christian:--Tychicus.

G5192.def: of uncertain derivation; the "hyacinth" or "jacinth", i.e. some gem of a deep blue color, probably the zirkon:-- jacinth.

G5194.et: perhaps from the same as (5205) (as being transparent like rain)
G5194.def: perhaps from the same as «5205» (as being transparent like rain); glass:--glass.

G5195.def: from «5196»; to exercise violence, i.e. abuse:--use despitefully, reproach, entreat shamefully (spitefully).

G5196.def: from «5228»; insolence (as over-bearing), i.e. insult, injury:--harm, hurt, reproach.

G5197.def: from «5195»; an insulter, i.e. maltreater:--despiteful, injurious.

G5198.def: from «5199»; to have sound health, i.e. be well (in body); figuratively, to be uncorrupt (true in doctrine):--be in health, (be safe and) sound, (be) whole(-some).

G5199.def: from the base of «837»; healthy, i.e. well (in body); figuratively, true (in doctrine):--sound, whole.
